title: Blade Runner 2099 Trailer Debuts at Comic-Con, Sets November Premiere on Prime Video
excerpt: Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer star in the sci-fi sequel series set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049, premiering all eight episodes on November 25.
body:
• Prime Video released the first trailer for Blade Runner 2099 at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, confirming a November 25 premiere for all eight episodes.
  • Michelle Yeoh stars as Olwen, a dying Replicant Blade Runner, alongside Hunter Schafer as Cora, a human fugitive posing as a Replicant to survive.
  • The limited series is set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049 in a Los Angeles where Replicants have won a war against humans and now rule society.
  • Showrunner Silka Luisa says the show explores what it means to be human in a world where humanity is no longer relevant.

Prime Video unveiled the first trailer for Blade Runner 2099 at its San Diego Comic-Con panel on Friday, giving fans their first proper look at the next chapter in Ridley Scott's four-decade-old sci-fi franchise. All eight episodes of the limited series will premiere on November 25.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0Dr8I_RyRCg

The teaser introduces a radically altered Los Angeles set half a century after the events of Denis Villeneuve's Blade Runner 2049. In this new timeline, the Replicant uprising that was brewing in the 2017 film has come to pass — and humans lost.

A World Turned Upside Down

"We already fought a war. We lost," Hunter Schafer's Cora says in the trailer. "Replicants — they keep taking it all away. How much longer until we have nothing? Until we are nothing?"

https://x.com/etnow/status/2080712132619039072

Schafer plays Cora, one of the few remaining humans, who has spent her life on the run, adopting new identities to survive in a society where Replicants are now the ruling class. In a final desperate bid, she takes on the most dangerous identity of all: a Blade Runner.

"The old world forever fights to come back. Humans want what was taken from them. But it's our time now."

— Michelle Yeoh as Olwen, Blade Runner 2099

Michelle Yeoh plays Olwen, a Replicant Blade Runner who is confronting the final days of her pre-programmed lifespan. Forced to partner with Cora, Olwen is hunting down a group of rogue Replicants hiding a truth that could destabilize the entire city.

"She's in the final days of her life, so she knows she has only days left to live because Replicants know down to the day when they're gonna die," showrunner Silka Luisa told Entertainment Weekly. "Her story is very much taking the Roy Batty story from the first film. We're telling it from the Replicant's point of view."

A Post-Human Los Angeles

The trailer reveals a Los Angeles that retains the franchise's signature visual DNA — towering cityscapes, hovering police spinners designed by Syd Mead, neon-soaked streets — but with a crucial twist. Humans are now the underclass. Replicants, physically and intellectually superior, have seized control of every institution.

Luisa described the premise during an EW profile published ahead of Comic-Con. "There's been a Replicant uprising that feels like it's been bubbling up. And between 2049 and 2099, that's happened," she said. "The Replicants are now the power brokers of the city. And humans are the second-class citizens."

The show's central question, according to Luisa: "What does it mean to be human in a world where humanity is no longer relevant?"

A Stacked Cast

Beyond its two leads, the series features Dimitri Abold (The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes), Lewis Gribben (Somewhere Boy), Katelyn Rose Downey (The Nun II), and Daniel Rigby (Renegade Nell). Recurring guest stars include Johnny Harris (A Gentleman in Moscow), Amy Lennox (Only Child), Sheila Atim (The Woman King), and Matthew Needham (House of the Dragon).

Ridley Scott, who directed the original 1982 Blade Runner, serves as executive producer alongside Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson of Alcon Television Group.

What to Watch For

The all-episodes-at-once release on November 25 marks Prime Video's bet that the franchise's devoted fanbase will treat the show as an event. The series is the first live-action Blade Runner television production and arrives more than four decades after Scott's original film, which was itself adapted from Philip K. Dick's 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

For diaspora audiences, the casting of Yeoh — an icon across Asian cinema — in a lead role is a notable draw, continuing her recent streak of prestige genre projects following her Oscar win for Everything Everywhere All at Once.
